An AWS architecture diagram is a visual representation of your cloud infrastructure on Amazon Web Services. It shows how AWS services connect and interact—from compute (EC2, Lambda) to storage (S3, RDS) to networking (VPC, CloudFront). Teams use AWS diagrams for planning (design infrastructure before deployment), documentation (record existing systems for compliance and onboarding), communication (explain architecture to stakeholders and team members), and troubleshooting (visualize data flow to identify bottlenecks). Whether you're architecting a simple web app or a complex microservices platform, an AWS diagram makes your infrastructure easier to understand. Common AWS Diagram Types VPC Network Diagrams Visualize your Virtual Private Cloud setup—subnets, route tables, security groups, NAT gateways, and internet gateways. Essential for understanding network isolation and traffic flow. Serverless Architecture Map Lambda functions, API Gateway endpoints, DynamoDB tables, and event triggers. Show how serverless components connect without managing servers. Three-Tier Web Architecture Classic web application design with load balancers (ALB/ELB), application servers (EC2/ECS), and database layer (RDS/Aurora). The foundation of most web applications. Data Pipeline Architecture Illustrate data flow through S3, Glue, Athena, Redshift, and analytics services. Critical for data engineering documentation.
